two_part_finding: Granting custody to a parent would be detrimental to the child
Granting custody to the nonparent is required to serve the best interest of the child
subdivision_a_default_gate.pleading_rule: Allegations of parental detriment, other than statement of the ultimate fact, shall not appear in the pleadings
subdivision_a_default_gate.hearing_closure: Court may exclude the public from the hearing on this issue

verbatim_factor_inventory.subdivision_b_clear_and_convincing: Parental-detriment finding supported by clear and convincing evidence, subject to (d) shift

elements: Physical and psychological needs for care and affection fulfilled

subdivision_d_preponderance_shift.trigger: Preponderance finding that proposed custodian meets (c)
subdivision_d_preponderance_shift.effect: Constitutes finding of best-interest + parental detriment absent preponderance rebuttal

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Map § 3041 against every nonparent-custody award or attempted award in the steward's 16-year record. For each, ask: (1) was there a clear-and-convincing detriment finding against a parent? (2) was nonparent custody found required — not merely preferred — for the child's best interest? (3) did the pleadings comply with (a)'s limitation rule? (4) if (d) was invoked, did the record contain explicit (c) findings (day-to-day role, both physical and psychological needs, substantial period)? (5) was any Indian-child analysis required under (e)?

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: For each nonparent-custody order of record, verify both the detriment finding and the 'required to serve' finding appear on the face of the order or in the record. A single-finding order is facially defective.
Verify the record reflects application of the clear-and-convincing standard (subject to (d) shift). Orders that apply preponderance without triggering (d) are defective.
Where (d) was invoked, verify the (c) predicate findings appear on the record. A bare (d) conclusion without the (c) predicate is defective.

Where the proposed nonparent custodian is (or was) a state employee whose institutional access fed the custody record, layer Evid. § 720 foundation attack + 42 U.S.C. § 1983 federal claim. § 3041 itself does not foreclose the posture; the surrounding law supplies the tools.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — ties directly to FAMLAW-005 (mother-as-dispatcher orchestration).

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Scan each nonparent-custody filing for pleaded detriment allegations beyond the ultimate fact. Filings that plead specific detriment facts are improper on their face and support motions to strike.
